# Agent notes

`just check` is not the merge gate. CI mutation-tests changed Rust lines in the kache binary. A PR that only ran `cargo test` on the new tests will go red on Mutation testing. That is the usual failure.

## Before `gh pr create`

```sh
just check
```

That is fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, and the workspace tests. Do not open the PR until it exits 0.

Mutants run in CI, not on your machine. Open the PR as a draft; the `Mutation testing (diff k/n)` shards test every changed Rust line in parallel on Linux runners and finish in well under an hour. A red shard prints the missed mutants in its log and uploads them as `missed.txt` in its `mutation-diff-report-<k>` artifact; add the test that kills each one, push, and mark the PR ready when every shard is green. A laptop running the same diff at one to three jobs takes hours and the load makes the fixture-based tests flake.

`just pr` still exists for a Linux box with cores to spare: it is `just check` plus `just mutants-diff` against `origin/main`, the same scope CI runs. If you use it:

```sh
cargo install --locked cargo-mutants --version 27.1.0
```

Do not invoke `cargo mutants` with `RUSTC_WRAPPER=kache`. The Justfile clears it. Hand-running mutants without `just` wraps kache in itself and the unmutated baseline dies.

## How mutants die here

Prefer tests and deleting dead branches over skip annotations.

- `if !s.is_empty() { print!("{s}") }` — printing `""` is a no-op, so `delete !` is missed. Call a helper that already has empty vs nonempty tests (`replay_cached_diagnostics`).
- `a && b` / `a || b` — one test where the left is false, one where the right is false.
- Named size constants built with `*` (`5 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024`) — do not `assert_eq!` against that same constant. Use an independent literal (`5 << 30`).
- `u64::try_from` on a value that is already `u64` — Linux clippy `-D warnings`. macOS clippy does not type-check `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]`.
- Unix-only test helpers under `-D warnings` on Windows are unused. Mark them `#[cfg(unix)]`.
- macOS-only helpers Linux never calls: `#[cfg(any(test, target_os = "macos"))]`.
- `Drop` / file locks — a second process must acquire after the first drops.
- New event-log fields — grep `event.schema` in the same commit and bump the tests.
- A test that passes is not a test that kills the mutant. Apply the mutation by hand, watch the test fail, then revert. A stale-record test passed under both `==` and `!=` because a single client refreshed its own record before the branch was ever reached; it took two clients to make the branch observable.
- Moving code without changing it still marks every moved line as changed, so the lane mutates lines your change never touched. Wrapping a 200-line block in a `loop` cost six survivors, four of them in code that predated the branch. Extract a function instead: the call site is one changed line and the body is none.
- Tests that read the live process environment race the rest of the suite, which mutates it (`set_env_for_test`). Take a snapshot and pass it in, or the test passes alone and fails in `just check`.

## PRs

Every PR targets `main`. Do not stack PRs on each other's branches. After one merges, rebase the others onto `main`.

Work in a git worktree. Do not mix unrelated dirty-tree WIP into the PR.

People keep running `cargo`. There is no `kache build`. Caching is `kache init` / `RUSTC_WRAPPER`.

---
name: codebase-memory
description: Use the codebase-memory knowledge graph for codebase exploration and structural code investigation. Invoke before any code task that requires locating or understanding unfamiliar code, behavior, structure, relationships, source matches, or change impact, especially when the exact file and symbol are not already known. Trigger for how or where code works; graph-ranked code search and bounded source retrieval; callers and callees; architecture, modules, entry points, dependencies, implementations, routes, data flow, cross-service links, affected code or tests, dead code, complexity, hotspots, refactor candidates, index coverage, ADR context, and custom Cypher.
---

# Codebase Memory

Tool only — mechanics, no workflow, no judgment.
Required standards — load before any step: none.

Start at the cheapest rung that can answer the question and stop the moment it does.

Invoke MCP tools when loaded; otherwise use the CLI below. Results go to **stdout**, diagnostics to
**stderr**: capture stdout, never discard stderr — it carries the rejection reason. Never pass the
global `--json`; it re-wraps the payload in an MCP envelope escaped as a string. The per-tool
`--format json` on `search_graph`, `trace_path`, `search_code` and `detect_changes` is real
structured output.

Read `references/binary-provenance.md` when a documented behaviour does not reproduce or the
binary was replaced.

Read `references/tool-contracts.md` when a call needs a parameter, limit, cursor, or failure mode
this file does not state, before `delete_project` or `manage_adr --mode update`, or during the
section-specific cases named below.

Substitute `<project>` from step 0 everywhere.

## 0. Orient — once per repo, per session, and after compaction

```bash
codebase-memory-mcp cli list_projects                                    # exact key + recorded root
codebase-memory-mcp cli index_status --project <project> --diagnostics summary # ready? gap samples?
```

`--diagnostics none` (the default) returns exact gap counts without samples; `summary` adds up to
five samples per category, and `full` adds up to 500. Add `--verbose true` only to debug where an
index lives.

Index only when absent, or when a large external update must be visible now:

```bash
codebase-memory-mcp cli --progress index_repository --repo-path <absolute-root>
```

## 1. Whole codebase → one module

```bash
codebase-memory-mcp cli get_architecture --project <project> --aspects structure   # rung 1
codebase-memory-mcp cli get_architecture --project <project>                       # rung 2
codebase-memory-mcp cli get_architecture --project <project> --path <subtree>      # scope any rung
```

Ask for the single aspect you need: `structure`, `dependencies`, `routes`, `hotspots`, `boundaries`,
`layers`, `clusters`, `file_tree`, `languages`, `packages`, `entry_points`, `overview`.
**Never `--aspects all`**, and omit `--aspects` rather than ask for `overview`.
`cycles` is opt-in and scans the whole call graph; request it solely for cycle analysis.
Read `references/tool-contracts.md` § Architecture aspects when reading `entry_points`, `routes`, or
`hotspots`.


## 2. Locate a symbol

```bash
codebase-memory-mcp cli search_graph --project <project> --name-pattern '<regex>' --limit 10  # regex
codebase-memory-mcp cli search_graph --project <project> --query '<words>' --limit 10         # BM25
```

Cost is linear in `--limit`; the default is 50, so always set it. Page only while `has_more`, with
`--offset`. Narrow with `--label`, `--file-pattern`, `--qn-pattern` before raising the limit.

- The two modes are exclusive: `--query` **ignores `--name-pattern`**.
- `--detail ids` drops metadata columns, is **silently ignored in `--query` mode**, and saves little
  regardless — narrow the query instead.
- `--semantic-query` takes an **array**: repeat the flag per keyword. Use only for vocabulary
  mismatch.
- Result `in`/`out` are selected relationship degree, **not caller counts**.
- BM25 ranks test files freely and `search_graph` has no test filter. `--file-pattern` is a
  glob/substring match with no negation — `^src/` silently matches nothing; positively match the
  production paths instead (`--file-pattern 'src/'`). `search_code --path-filter`, by contrast, *is*
  a regex.
- Add `--fields complexity --fields cognitive` (also `signature`, `docstring`, `return_type`,
  `is_test`, `lines`) for refactor and hotspot triage.
- `--include-connected true` adds a `connected` column naming a linked symbol per row — a one-call
  orientation hop when you need each hit's nearest relation without a separate `trace_path`.
- Dead-code sweep: `--label Function --max-degree 0 --exclude-entry-points true`. Without `--label`
  the result is dominated by config and YAML nodes. Treat hits as candidates only. `OVERRIDE` edges
  (implementation → trait) count toward degree, so `--label Method` degree-0 hits are zero-edge
  forwarding stubs, not trait impls.

## 3. Read source

```bash
codebase-memory-mcp cli get_code_snippet --project <project> --qualified-name <short-or-full-name>
```

Short names resolve by suffix match, so skip step 2 when the name is likely unique; an ambiguous
name returns `status: ambiguous` with suggestions, never a wrong symbol. Oversized callables return
a bounded page plus `next_cursor`; follow it with identical arguments until `source_complete=true`.
Anchor the first page with `--focus-line`. **Oversized** Module and Class nodes return a structural
outline — request `--start-line`/`--end-line` inside the symbol for raw source; small ones return
source directly. Address a whole file by its **Module** node (`<project>.<path.to.module>` resolves
by suffix and returns the outline). There is no `.__file__` node: that name returns
`symbol not found` with exit 1. `--include-neighbors true` only when immediate relationships matter.
`--max-response-bytes` defaults to 24576 and is validated, never clamped: outside 2048-65536 you get
empty stdout, a non-zero exit, and the range on stderr.

Snippet source is ground truth even when `coverage_note` warns the graph may be incomplete.

## 4. Callers, callees, blast radius

```bash
codebase-memory-mcp cli trace_path --project <project> --function-name <name> \
    --direction inbound --depth 1 --limit 10                              # rung 1
```

Always pass `--direction` and `--depth`; they default to `both` and `3`. Use `both` only when
cross-service callers matter. `--depth` is capped at 15 (`CBM_MCP_MAX_DEPTH`) on `trace_path` and
`detect_changes`; a value above 15 is **rejected** with `depth must be at most 15 (given N)` on
stderr and no trace.

Determine sufficient depth by frontier growth, not a flag: within 1–15 the trace never signals that
it hit the ceiling. Raise `--depth` a hop at a time and read `callers_total`/`callees_total` each
time; when the total stops moving, the traversal has reached the graph's natural edge and is
complete. Only when the total is *still climbing at depth 15* is the cap the binding constraint —
then raise it with `CBM_MCP_MAX_DEPTH=<n>`, no reindex needed.

Read `references/tool-contracts.md` § Change impact when starting from a Git diff instead of a
symbol.

- `--include-tests true` is required for dead-code, deletion, and exhaustive-usage claims; tests are
  excluded by default. Keep the default when the question is who in *production* calls this.
- `--mode data_flow` for argument flow. `--mode cross_service` traverses in-project HTTP/async/data
  flow through Routes **plus** `CROSS_*` cross-repo edges — use it freely for "what does this call
  over HTTP", it works on a single project. Only the `CROSS_*` half needs projects linked at index
  time (`index_repository --mode cross-repo-intelligence --target-projects`); unlinked, in-project
  hops still resolve while cross-repo hops return clean empty, which is not evidence of absence.
  Read `references/tool-contracts.md` § Index modes and
  cross-repository setup when linking projects for a cross-repo trace.
- Treat CALLS edges as candidates: add `--include-evidence true` and confirm the call site in
  source before acting on a surprising edge.

## 5. Text search

```bash
codebase-memory-mcp cli search_code --project <project> --pattern '<literal>' --mode files --limit 10
codebase-memory-mcp cli search_code --project <project> --pattern '<literal>' --limit 10  # compact
codebase-memory-mcp cli search_code --project <project> --pattern '<regex>' --regex true --limit 10
```

**`--regex` defaults to false**, which matches whitespace-separated terms *in order but not
adjacently*, treating metacharacters literally. Pass `--regex true` only when you want regex
semantics. On a literal containing metacharacters it silently misfires: `[ ]`, `*` and `|` collapse
to `raw_matches=0 scan=complete` (`|` is matched as a byte, not alternation; the result then carries
`warning_literal_pipe` — read it). Always check `raw_matches` against expectation — a zero still
reports `scan=complete`.

There is no cursor: narrow `--path-filter`
(regex), `--file-pattern` (glob), or the pattern. Use native grep for anything under
`not_indexed` — `search_code` scans indexed files only and still reports
`scan=complete`.

## 6. Custom structural questions

```bash
codebase-memory-mcp cli get_graph_schema --project <project>
codebase-memory-mcp cli query_graph --project <project> --query '<cypher with LIMIT>'
```

Cypher goes in `--query`, not `--cypher`. Read `references/tool-contracts.md` § Cypher when
writing any query.

Read stored architecture decisions before assuming none exist:

```bash
codebase-memory-mcp cli manage_adr --project <project> --mode sections   # headings only
codebase-memory-mcp cli manage_adr --project <project>                   # full document
```

`ingest_traces` is a stub: it accepts input and creates no edges, so the graph holds no runtime-call
edges.

## Before any negative or exhaustive claim

Read `references/tool-contracts.md` § Negative and exhaustive claims when claiming "does not
exist", "unused", "dead", "all callers", "only caller", "nothing implements this", a deletion
is safe, or a complete blast radius or impact.

## Handing off

Pass the project key, indexed Git context, bounded scope, qualified symbols, queries and pagination
state, verified source, and coverage gaps. A child without graph tools must not claim it queried the
graph.

description: |
  Rules for test code in any language: what a test must prove, how its red is earned,
  which tooling decides coverage, and the boundary between test and production code.
  Load before writing, strengthening, deleting, or reviewing a test, before judging
  whether a test is worth keeping, and before interpreting a coverage or mutation
  result. Standards only — no workflow, no role. Production-code rules live in

  cues: "write a test", "add a test", "cover this", "flaky test", "weak test",
  "mutation run", "coverage".

# Testing standards

Standards only — no workflow, no role.
Required standards — load before any step: `coding-standards` (seam costs for the
test-level rule).

## Judgment

- A small-edit breakage is a change to one operator, constant, branch condition, call,
  or ordering in the code under test that would not obviously fail compilation or an
  unrelated existing test. "Regression" and "breakage" in this skill mean that shape.
- A search or discriminator a command can settle is run, never reasoned about.
- Where a rule requires drafting or naming something no procedure fully determines, the
  answer is recorded verbatim in the report; silence is never an outcome.
- **Escape hatch.** No consumer of this skill blocks a run or asks a mid-run question.
  An element evidence cannot settle becomes an `ambiguity` record — what was checked
  (commands quoted), what remains unsettled, what evidence would settle it — and the run
  continues. An ambiguity record is a complete result.
- Read `references/oracle-and-vacuity.md` when choosing a test's oracle, doubles, or
  level, or checking a test for vacuity.
- Read `references/gap-finding.md` when claiming or refuting a coverage gap or a
  duplicate test, enumerating what a scope must test, or ranking findings.
- Read `references/verdict.md` when ruling a test KEEP, REDO, or REMOVE, or reading a
  mutation-sweep result against a test.

## Boundary

- A test task edits test files only — no production edit of any kind. A production
  change a test seems to need is filed through the defect-filing route the brief or the
  repo's AGENTS.md names, never made.
- A test never asks production for surface it does not otherwise need: no error variant,
  accessor, visibility widening, observability field, or `#[cfg(test)]` hook added so a
  test can see inside. It asserts the observable contract instead.

## Red

- A test's executed red comes from the mutation lane or from a recorded red-first run —
  the test ran and failed before the behaviour existed — never from a hand breakage. The
  mutation lane is the repo's mutation tool, as its AGENTS.md names, run as a batch
  sweep outside any test task, which neither launches the tool nor waits on its result.
  Each new or strengthened test instead carries stated oracle reasoning — what the
  assertion pins and why it cannot pass vacuously — and the sweep supplies the executed
  breakage evidence later.
- Oracle reasoning names its discriminator: the fixture input or state under which the
  assertion fails if the property does not hold. Execute it — set the fixture to that
  value, run, record the observed failure, restore the fixture, and run again green;
  both runs go in the report. This varies the fixture, never the code under test, so it
  is not a hand breakage.
- A discriminator that cannot be made to fail means the fixture cannot vary the property:
  widen the fixture or choose a different oracle, and never report the test as proven.
  The exception is a property no fixture value can vary because it is structural — field
  declaration order, trait impl presence, a lint's own registration. Name it as
  structural in the report, state which tool operator would have covered it and that none
  does, and report the test as unproven-by-execution.
- A sweep survivor inside a test's target is a finding that returns to a fresh test task;
  it is never silenced with a test that pins the mutant's exact shape.

## Coverage

- Coverage is a verdict the tooling returns after the tests exist: the writer aims at
  the named obligations and reads coverage afterwards, never at a coverage number.

## Test shape

- One behaviour per test. A test that asserts on two unrelated outcomes is two tests.
- Test names state the behaviour and the expected outcome in plain words.

## Fixtures and flake

- A test never touches host state: no live data store, no user-level tool config, no real
  home directory. Fixtures are created by the test and destroyed by it. The repo's
  AGENTS.md names the mechanics.
- A test that fails intermittently gets at most two re-runs; then read its source for the
  deadline or race. "Passed on retry" is not a cause.
- A test shares no process-global state with its siblings. A test that captures
  telemetry asserts on the structured output of an isolated process. Read
  `references/rust-telemetry.md` when a Rust test touches process-global state or
  captures telemetry. Retire this bullet when a lint rejects in-process telemetry
  capture in test code.

name: coding-standards
description: |
  Shape rules for production code in any language, with the thresholds a lint enforces.
  Load before writing, editing, refactoring, or reviewing production code; before adding a

  rename, or removal of a compatibility layer. Standards only — no workflow, no role.

---

# Coding standards

Standards only — no workflow, no role.
Required standards — load before any step: none.

## Size

- A function stays within the repo's size lint at the tool's default threshold (Rust:
  `clippy::too_many_lines` 100 lines, `clippy::cognitive_complexity` 25; Python: ruff
  `PLR0915`, `C901`; TypeScript: eslint `max-lines-per-function`, `complexity`). Over →
  extract the named sub-step. Never add a suppression. A size-lint baseline entry whose
  function is under the limit is deleted in the change that finds it. Never split one
  body into two functions that are meaningless apart.
- Nesting deeper than four levels → invert the condition or extract the inner block.

## Existence

- A new function, predicate, decoder, or validator exists only after a code-graph search
  on its behaviour found no existing one. The query, its hit count, and the reason any
  hit was not reused go in the commit body. Found → call the existing one, extending its
  signature if needed. Not found → write it once, at the lowest module every caller can
  reach.
- A trait, generic parameter, builder, or witness/proof type — anything that adds
  indirection — is kept with two production consumers, inlined to the concrete type and
  the plain function with one, deleted with none. Two exemptions: a validated-constructor
  newtype, whose second consumer is the input it rejects; and a port at a hexagonal I/O
  seam (§Shape), whose second consumer is the test fake that lets the core run without
  the adapter.
- An error enum variant exists only where a production caller branches on it (`match`,
  `if let`, `matches!`). The distinguishing detail rides in the message (§Boundary
  correctness), not in a new variant.
- A guard for a state the types or the schema already exclude is deleted, not tested.
  A precondition enforced upstream is encoded in the type at the seam, never re-checked.
- Two functions that differ only in a type name become one generic or one function over
  a trait the two types share — when both encode one contract that a change to one must
  also make to the other. Same shape, different owning contract, stays two functions.
- A function or variant with zero production consumers is deleted in the change that
  finds it, unless it is public API with an external consumer.

## Shape

- Hexagonal (dependency inversion): the domain core depends only on ports it owns; every
  I/O (network, filesystem, clock, UI, provider) sits behind an adapter, so the core is
  testable without the adapter.
- A module boundary (single responsibility) exists where two external contracts the code
  itself binds — a wire type, a schema, a vendor API's types, a config file's keys, a
  public signature — change independently and the seam between them costs no shared
  mutable state, no bidirectional call, and at most one added indirection. Each contract
  is cited at the line that binds it; a prose document describing one may explain a
  boundary, never establish it. "Does two things", "is long", or "looks like two topics"
  places no boundary. What a crossing costs per language, and which languages' tests
  reach a unit's privates: read `references/language-cost-model.md` when pricing a
  boundary or choosing a test level.
- Knowledge — a policy, message, format, formula, or key — is written once and read
  from that one place (DRY, single source of truth). Two copies that must change together
  are one defect.
- An implementation keeps its interface's contract (Liskov substitution); an interface
  carries only what its consumers call (interface segregation); new behaviour extends
  a seam instead of editing callers (open/closed).
- Encode every guarantee the language can express in types: invalid states
  unrepresentable, validated constructors over raw primitives.
- A name that misstates what its item does → rename it in the change that finds it.

## Comments

- A comment exists only where the code cannot say it: a non-obvious WHY, an invariant the
  reader would otherwise break, a workaround with the bug or spec that forced it, its id
  in the `//!` block.
- A spec or ticket id (`ADR-n`, `REQ-n`, `ISSUE-n`, `TASK-n`) appears once, in the file's
  leading module doc block (`//!`), never inside a function body. A `// TRADE-OFF:`
  comment naming a displaced enforcement tier is the one body exception.
- Doc comments on public items carry the contract (inputs, outputs, errors, invariants).
  A doc comment that restates the name, narrates the decision's history, or cites clause
  numbers is cut.

## Boundary correctness

- Reject, don't coerce: input the program cannot use exactly as given is refused with an
  error whose message names source, key, given, expected — never clamped, defaulted, or
  repaired. Tolerance only at a boundary you do not own both sides of.
- Read `references/tooling.md` when writing a script, a wrapper, or a tool another agent
  consumes.

## Change discipline

- Write in the idiom of the repo's stack as the wider ecosystem practises it today, never
  training-data defaults and never local convention that contradicts the ecosystem.
- Rewrite the pattern you were already changing rather than patch it. An incidental
  defect elsewhere is fixed in place only when all four hold: the fix is one hunk, it
  touches no signature, its test is in the same change, and the repo's own instructions
  or specs already determine the correct behaviour; otherwise file it through the
  defect-filing route the brief or the repo's AGENTS.md names.
- No shim, compat layer, or old path survives a change to code you control: the change
  is done only when every internal caller uses the new shape and the old one is deleted.
  Carve-out only where you do not own both sides.
- Unstaged or untracked files you did not produce → halt and surface before committing.

## Review

Read `references/review.md` when reviewing or auditing production code.

## Tools

- Code navigation — locating symbols, callers, structure, impact — goes through the
  repo's code-graph index; `rg`/`fd` are for text, configs, and non-code files only.
- A repo with no package manager chosen: Python `uv`, Node.js `pnpm`; otherwise the
  repo's.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run a test-bearing command with enough file descriptors for Kache's parallel
# suite. Low Unix soft limits can otherwise surface unrelated policy failures
# when filesystem operations fail closed under EMFILE (#756).
set -euo pipefail

target_nofile=4096
fallback_max_threads=8

if [ "$#" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "usage: $0 <command> [args...]" >&2
  exit 64
fi

is_positive_integer() {
  [[ "$1" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]
}

limit_is_sufficient() {
  local limit="$1"
  if [ "$limit" = "unlimited" ]; then
    return 0
  fi
  is_positive_integer "$limit" && ((10#$limit >= target_nofile))
}

available_test_threads() {
  local detected
  detected="$(getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if is_positive_integer "$detected"; then
    printf '%s\n' "$detected"
  else
    # Unknown is not permission to increase concurrency. One is the only
    # conservative fallback when the host cannot report its CPU allowance.
    printf '1\n'
  fi
}

# Windows has no POSIX RLIMIT_NOFILE. Git Bash can execute this wrapper for
# local Just recipes, but the command itself should remain native there.
case "$(uname -s 2>/dev/null || true)" in
  CYGWIN* | MINGW* | MSYS*) exec "$@" ;;
esac

soft_nofile="$(ulimit -Sn 2>/dev/null || true)"
if limit_is_sufficient "$soft_nofile"; then
  exec "$@"
fi

if ulimit -Sn "$target_nofile" 2>/dev/null; then
  raised_nofile="$(ulimit -Sn 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if limit_is_sufficient "$raised_nofile"; then
    exec "$@"
  fi
fi

# A builder may have a hard limit below 4096. Bound libtest only in that case;
# never raise an explicit setting or the host's available parallelism.
available_threads="$(available_test_threads)"
fallback_threads="$available_threads"
if [ "${RUST_TEST_THREADS+x}" = "x" ]; then
  if ! is_positive_integer "$RUST_TEST_THREADS"; then
    echo "invalid RUST_TEST_THREADS=$RUST_TEST_THREADS: expected a positive integer" >&2
    exit 64
  fi
  fallback_threads="$RUST_TEST_THREADS"
fi
if ((10#$fallback_threads > 10#$available_threads)); then
  fallback_threads="$available_threads"
fi
if ((10#$fallback_threads > fallback_max_threads)); then
  fallback_threads="$fallback_max_threads"
fi
export RUST_TEST_THREADS="$fallback_threads"

printf \
  'warning: could not raise soft nofile limit %s to %s; capping Rust test threads at %s\n' \
  "${soft_nofile:-unknown}" "$target_nofile" "$fallback_threads" >&2
exec "$@"
[package]
name = "kache"
version = "1.1.1"
edition = "2024"
description = "Compiler cache for Rust, C/C++ and CUDA, with S3, GCS, shared-filesystem and OCI remotes."
license = "Apache-2.0"
repository = "https://github.com/kunobi-ninja/kache"
homepage = "https://kunobi.ninja/docs/kache"
keywords = ["build-cache", "rustc-wrapper", "blake3", "cargo"]
categories = ["development-tools::build-utils", "caching"]
rust-version = "1.95"

[workspace]
members = [
    "crates/kache-core",
    "crates/kache-format",
    "crates/kache-fs",
    "crates/kache-shims",
    "crates/kache-store",
    "crates/kache-e2e",
    "crates/kache-proofs",
    "crates/kache-service",
]
# scenarios/e2e-*/source and test-projects/* are not listed: each declares its own empty
# `[workspace]` so cargo treats them as standalone, which is what the
# e2e harness (and the integration tests) need to drive them as
# realistic standalone consumers of kache.
#
# `tmp/` is the bench and e2e scratch tree, where third-party subjects are
# cloned. A subject that is itself a workspace root (substrate, opendal) stops
# cargo's upward walk on its own, but a plain single-package subject (jdx/hk)
# does not, and cargo then refuses to build it: "current package believes it's
# in a workspace when it's not". We do not control those manifests, so exclude
# the directory they land in.
exclude = ["tmp"]
resolver = "3"

[dependencies]
foldhash = "0.2"
kunobi-daemon = { version = "0.9.0", features = ["wire-async", "local-async", "launch"] }
kache-format = { version = "1.1.1", path = "crates/kache-format" }
kache-fs = { version = "1.1.1", path = "crates/kache-fs" }
kache-store = { version = "1.1.1", path = "crates/kache-store" }
kache-shims = { version = "1.1.1", path = "crates/kache-shims" }
blake3 = "1"
bytes = "1"
# OpenDAL publishes its modules as separate crates. Depending on only the
# core, S3, filesystem, retry, and reqwest transport modules keeps Kache's
# supported backend set explicit and avoids compiling unused services.
opendal = { package = "opendal-core", version = "=0.59.3", default-features = false, features = ["executors-tokio"] }
opendal-http-transport-reqwest = { version = "=0.59.3", default-features = false, features = ["rustls-no-provider"] }
opendal-layer-retry = { version = "=0.59.3", default-features = false }
opendal-service-fs = { version = "=0.59.3", default-features = false }
opendal-service-s3 = { version = "=0.59.3", default-features = false }
opendal-service-gcs = { version = "=0.59.3", default-features = false }
oci-client = { version = "0.18", default-features = false, features = ["rustls-tls-no-provider"] }
docker_credential = "1.3"
sha2 = "0.11"
hex = "0.4"
# OpenDAL exposes a custom credential chain but not a profile-name shortcut.
# These published reqsign APIs preserve Kache's explicit profile selection
# (including SSO and credential_process) without a git-only patch.
reqsign-aws-v4 = { version = "=3.3.1", default-features = false }
reqsign-core = { version = "=3.3.2", default-features = false }
# Direct dep so OpenDAL/reqwest can use ring without reintroducing aws-lc.
rustls = { version = "0.23", default-features = false, features = ["ring"] }
kache-core = { version = "1.1.1", path = "crates/kache-core", default-features = false, features = ["planning"] }
async-trait = "0.1"
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["rt", "rt-multi-thread", "macros", "process", "fs", "io-util", "net", "time", "signal", "sync"] }
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"
semver = "1"
base64 = "0.23"
toml = "1"
clap = { version = "4", features = ["derive"] }
clap_complete = "4"
rusqlite = { version = "0.40", features = ["bundled"] }
ratatui = "0.30"
crossterm = "0.29"
filetime = "0.2"
anyhow = "1"
tracing = "0.1"
tracing-subscriber = { version = "0.3", features = ["env-filter", "fmt", "registry"] }
zstd = "0.14"
bytesize = "2"
chrono = { version = "0.4", features = ["serde"] }
dirs = "7"
home = "0.5.12"
tar = "0.4"
futures = "0.3"
glob = "0.3"
libc = "0.2"
memchr = "2"
tempfile = "3"
reqwest = { version = "0.13", default-features = false, features = ["json", "rustls-no-provider"] }
# `kache login` and planner bearer sessions. The -core features keep reqwest
# on `rustls-no-provider`, so ring stays the only TLS provider (no aws-lc).
kunobi-auth = { version = "1.0.0", default-features = false, features = ["client-core", "browser-login-core", "rust_crypto"] }
interprocess = { version = "2.4.4", features = ["tokio"] }
unicode-normalization = "0.1"
# Used by `src/compiler/flags.rs` (the cc / future Swift / future MSVC
# flag classifier). The `regex` crate is linear-time by construction
# (no backtracking, no lookarounds) — matters because the wrapper runs
# the classifier on every cc compile argument; bounded cost is a design
# requirement.
regex = { version = "1", default-features = false, features = ["std", "perf"] }
regex-automata = { version = "0.4", default-features = false, features = ["std", "syntax", "meta", "nfa-pikevm"] }

[target.'cfg(windows)'.dependencies]
# `#[mutants::skip]` on the Win32 volume query. The attribute is a no-op;
# cargo-mutants reads it so a body Linux never compiles is not a survivor.
mutants = "0.0.4"
# Use the same Visual Studio and Windows SDK discovery path as Rust build
# tooling, including shells where VsDevCmd has not populated PATH/LIB.
find-msvc-tools = "0.1.12"
# `pure` drops blake3's C SIMD (`c/blake3_neon.c` / SSE intrinsics), whose
# arm64 NEON path doesn't cross-compile under cargo-xwin's clang + MSVC
# sysroot. Windows-only so native/Linux/macOS keep the fast C SIMD backend.
blake3 = { version = "1", features = ["pure"] }
windows-sys = { version = "0.61", features = [
    "Win32_Foundation",
    "Win32_System_Threading",
    "Win32_Storage_FileSystem",
    # ReFS block-cloning (FSCTL_DUPLICATE_EXTENTS_TO_FILE) for zero-copy,
    # write-isolated restore on a Dev Drive — see link::try_reflink (#429).
    "Win32_System_IO",
    "Win32_System_Ioctl",
    # FILE_SUPPORTS_BLOCK_REFCOUNTING — ask the volume whether it block-clones
    # instead of inferring "no CoW" from one failed clone (#508).
    "Win32_System_SystemServices",
    # `kache test-runner` leaves Ctrl-C to the test it runs.
    "Win32_System_Console",
] }

[dev-dependencies]
kache-store = { version = "1.1.1", path = "crates/kache-store", features = ["test-support"] }
kache-fs = { version = "1.1.1", path = "crates/kache-fs", features = ["testing"] }
assert_cmd = "2"
axum = "0.8"
predicates = "3"
proptest = { version = "1.11.0", default-features = false, features = ["std", "handle-panics"] }
serde_json = "1"
bytes = "1"

# `{ archive-suffix }` resolves from each target's pkg-fmt (".tar.gz" for
# tgz, ".zip" for zip) — never hardcode the extension here: the release
# workflow (_release-rust.yml) packages Windows targets as .zip and
# everything else as .tar.gz (see #311). Guarded by
# tests/binstall_metadata_test.rs.
[package.metadata.binstall]
pkg-url = "{ repo }/releases/download/v{ version }/{ name }-{ target }{ archive-suffix }"
pkg-fmt = "tgz"

[package.metadata.binstall.overrides.x86_64-pc-windows-msvc]
pkg-fmt = "zip"

[package.metadata.binstall.overrides.aarch64-pc-windows-msvc]
pkg-fmt = "zip"

# Debian packaging (cargo-deb). Read by the _workflows build_deb step to
# produce kache_<version>_{amd64,arm64}.deb, which package-publish.yml then
# pushes into the apt repo on R2. cargo-deb reads this regardless of the
# --target passed, so the same config drives both amd64 and arm64 builds.
[package.metadata.deb]
maintainer = "Kunobi Ninja <feedback@kunobi.ninja>"
copyright = "2026, Zondax AG"
license-file = ["LICENSE", "0"]
extended-description = """\
kache is a zero-copy, content-addressed build cache for Rust, C/C++ and more. \
It avoids file \
copies and wasted disk by hardlinking artifacts locally and sharing them \
via S3-compatible object storage or a shared filesystem."""
section = "utils"
priority = "optional"
# CRITICAL: empty depends. kache is built as a static musl binary, so it has
# no shared-library runtime dependencies. An auto-resolved or non-empty
# `depends` would pin glibc and break install on musl/minimal systems.
depends = ""
assets = [
    ["target/release/kache", "usr/bin/kache", "755"],
    ["README.md", "usr/share/doc/kache/README", "644"],
]
# postinst runs `kache init --shims /usr/lib/kache --force --canonical-only`
# so the farm matches SHIM_NAMES in this binary. prerm removes those links.
maintainer-scripts = "packaging/debian/"

[profile.dev]
debug = 0
strip = "symbols"

[profile.release]
debug = 0
lto = "fat"
codegen-units = 1
strip = "symbols"

[lints.rust]
warnings = "deny"

[lints.clippy]
permissions_set_readonly_false = "allow"
too_many_arguments = "allow"

---
name: verification-standards
description: |
  What "done" means for a unit of code work in any language, and how the verdict is
  reported. Load before declaring a task complete, before reviewing another agent's
  completed work, before accepting a dispatch report, and before merging a branch.
  Standards only — no workflow, no role; the verifier and the orchestrator load the same
  file. Production-code rules live in `coding-standards`; test rules in
  `testing-standards`; the repo's own commands (test runner, mutation tool, commit gate)
  are named in its AGENTS.md. Trigger on bare cues: "is this done", "verify", "review the
  branch", "ready to merge", "accept the report", "PASS/FAIL".
---

# Verification standards

Standards only — no workflow, no role.
Required standards — load before any step: `coding-standards` and `testing-standards`
(every check in §Shape and §Tests is one of their rules, re-checked here), and
`codebase-memory` (the queries §Shape re-runs).

## Verdict

- A unit of work is PASS only when every check below holds; any one failing is FAIL with
  that check named. There is no partial pass.
- A verifier that proves an in-scope defect records FAIL at the audited SHA, then
  continues as its fixer while the causal context is fresh. It follows the repository's
  production or test authoring discipline for the repair and lists the resulting commits;
  when both production and test work are required, keep their ownership and commits
  distinct. Do not bounce a proved defect back to a context-soaked previous author.
- The edit band is any single-site fix whose correctness a probe this same verifier has
  ALREADY EXECUTED demonstrates: the fix flips that probe red→green without restructuring
  the predicate or the oracle. A fix needing a re-derived predicate, a new oracle, or a
  probe not yet run is structural — report it as a finding and route it back to the owning
  role. A verifier that redesigns has no independent check on its redesign.
- A fixer never verifies its own changes. After the repair, a fresh independent verifier
  audits the new tip. A finding is returned without repair only when it falls outside the
  edit band above, exceeds the accepted scope, requires authority the verifier lacks, or
  remains genuinely underdetermined after the required evidence work.
- Finding nothing is a valid result, reported as PASS with the list of what was checked.

## Evidence — what licenses each claim

- "Implements the task" — each acceptance criterion the task names is paired with the
  test that proves it (file:line) or the command whose output shows it. A criterion with
  neither is unmet.
- "Tests pass" — the repo's targeted test command and its summary line, run at the
  verified SHA. A green from memory or from a prior run is not evidence.
- "Covered" — the repo's mutation tool's verdict line on the diff, or the repo's stated
  exemption quoted. Survivors listed as file:line + mutation.
- "Gate green" — the repo's commit gate ran on the verified commit and exited 0. A commit
  that bypassed the gate is FAIL regardless of other evidence.
- "No regression" — the targeted suites named, with their summary lines at the verified
  SHA.
- Every claim cites a file:line, a command with its output, or a graph query with its
  result. A claim with none of those is absent from the verdict.

## Shape — re-checking the `coding-standards` rules a lint cannot

- Each of the `coding-standards` skill's Size, Existence, Shape, and Comments rules is
  re-checked on the diff, and the result is a line in the report.
- Where the rule rests on a graph query — the reuse search in a commit body, the
  consumer count of a new indirection, the caller that branches on a new variant — the
  verifier re-runs it (`trace_path` inbound for consumers) at the verified SHA. A
  missing query, a hit neither reused nor rejected with a reason in the commit body, or
  a consumer count the rule does not permit, is FAIL. A test-only consumer counts only
  where the rule's exemption names it.

## Tests — re-checking the `testing-standards` rules

- Each new test's report carries the oracle reasoning and the executed discriminator
  the `testing-standards` skill requires: the fixture value varied, the observed
  failure, and the green run on the restored fixture. Either absent is FAIL.
- Each of the `testing-standards` skill's Boundary and Fixtures rules is re-checked on
  the diff.

## Report

- First line: `PASS` or `FAIL: <the check that failed, quoted from this file>`.
- Then, in order: commit SHA verified; commands run with summary lines; criteria → proof
  table; findings as file:line + one sentence + severity (blocks merge / fix before next
  dispatch / note); fixes made after a FAIL and the fresh-verifier handoff required; what
  was checked and found correct.
- At most 12 lines before the findings; no narrative of the verification process.
- A defect outside the verified diff is filed through the defect-filing route the brief
  or the repo's AGENTS.md names, with file:line and one sentence, is listed by id in the
  report, and does not change the verdict.

No cache implementation was modified. Reproduce in a fresh process: `env KACHE_FLAKY_HOME=1 K test_is_macos_protected -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture`. One forced failure in one invocation; R16 passed in a fresh process without that initialization. Forced-run load: `{ 43.84 66.49 50.05 }`.

Fix shape: test the classification core with explicit home/prefix inputs; test process-wide initialization in isolated subprocesses with a deliberately fixed HOME. Comparing a cache initialized by an earlier caller against the current ambient HOME leaves run order in the oracle.

@@FAIL_R11@@

**6. Proven: `daemon::tests::test_wait_for_warming_blocks_then_signals`, `src/daemon/tests.rs:10544`. Class: wall-clock upper-bound assertion under descheduling. Severity: medium.**

The signal task sleeps 50 ms at line 10551. The waiter has a five-second grace at line 10556, but the test also requires elapsed time below one second at line 10560. `wait_for_warming`, `src/daemon.rs:3268`, returns the watch-channel completion state, or observes a change under the requested timeout. A CPU scheduling pause can consume the test'"'s one-second allowance without breaking that mechanism or exhausting the five-second grace.

R20 emitted a PID marker immediately after the original timer started, then the external controller sent SIGSTOP only to that test process, waited 1.2 seconds, and sent SIGCONT. The existing warming-result assertion passed, and the existing "'`elapsed < 1s` assertion failed. Reproduce by applying phase-3 instrumentation and running `python3 /private/tmp/kache-flaky/sol/run.py R20-repro python3 /private/tmp/kache-flaky/sol/suspend.py`. The controller invokes `env KACHE_FLAKY_SUSPEND=1 K test_wait_for_warming_blocks_then_signals -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture`. One valid forced failure in one invocation, load `{ 26.51 43.46 46.73 }`. R15 and the subsequent uninstrumented workspace runs provide controls.

R10'"'s preliminary probe added an await before the timer and failed the lower bound. That is **not** counted as proof: the original default current-thread Tokio runtime has no yield between spawning the signal task and starting the timer. R20 preserves that original scheduling structure and proves the upper-bound problem by pausing the process externally.

Fix shape: establish a pending warming future, signal completion, and assert it resolves successfully. Exercise timeout behavior with virtual Tokio time or explicit clock input. The mechanism does not require a real-machine one-second speed assertion.

If that optional probe cannot identify the server, kache tries the fallback and then recovers through the direct compiler—the sequence shown in the failure. Seven tests have demonstrated dependencies on scheduling, the live process environment, or process-wide initialization. Two findings assert elapsed clock bounds, two use sleeps as synchronization, two depend on shared process state, and one assumes an optional external probe meets a deadline. The known cache-key failure is a shared-process-state race. The owner's clock hypothesis explains some findings, but does not explain all of them.

Investigation: detached `991c83694c056119d8eba8f9c1f376ac246efb52`, macOS arm64, one investigator, no subagents. No fixes, commits, pushes, PRs, issues, or mutation runs. Temporary source instrumentation was restored; its complete diffs are included below. The report is saved at [report.md](/private/tmp/kache-flaky/sol/report.md); test logs and the run ledger are in the same directory. Test execution ran from 01:36:48 to 02:28:20 UTC on 2026-10-14, stopping at ten full-workspace commands.

All cargo invocations inherited `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/kache-flaky/sol/target`. The normal libtest default was 16 threads on this machine; explicit thread counts are recorded per run. The shell's soft nofile limit was 1,048,576, above the wrapper's 4,096 requirement. Load entries are the verbatim output of `sysctl -n vm.loadavg` immediately before each invocation, giving the 1-, 5-, and 15-minute averages; they are not measurements throughout the run.

For compact reproduction commands and the run table, `W` expands to `./scripts/with-test-resources.sh cargo test --workspace`, and `K` expands to `./scripts/with-test-resources.sh cargo test -p kache --bin kache`. Execute these from the worktree with the target directory exported. Commands requiring instrumentation use the corresponding patch below.

**1. Proven: `compiler::cc::tests::terminal_formatting_shares_cc_keys_with_cold_and_warm_probes`, [src/compiler/cc/tests.rs:250](/Users/viktor/Developer/github/kache-investigations/flaky-sol/src/compiler/cc/tests.rs:250). Class: shared process state, environment and current directory. Severity: high.**

The test computes the baseline at line 285 and compares cold and warm keys at lines 295 and 299 without taking the process-state lock. Every key reads ambient state again: `src/compiler/cc.rs:4389` builds its prefix-map identity from cwd, `KACHE_CC_PATH_NORMALIZE`, `KACHE_BASE_DIR`, `SDKROOT`, and `OUT_DIR`; line 4432 recomputes maps. A nonempty SDK contributes `/kache/sdkroot` at line 4628. Key generation hashes the distinct prefix-map sentinels at line 6933 and mapped source paths at line 7108. Changing normalization changes both of those inputs. The fake compiler at `tests/fixtures/mock_cc_diagnostics.sh:3` returns constant version/preprocessor output and echoes the already filtered probe arguments; it contains no clock-dependent output.

Sibling writers are concrete: `src/compiler/cc/tests.rs:6985` sets SDKROOT and line 6990 removes it; the environment/normalization test at line 7962 changes cwd, OUT_DIR, SDKROOT, and the normalization switch at lines 7983, 7996, and 8009. The shared lock at `src/test_support.rs:83` coordinates participating tests only. `set_env_for_test`, `src/config/tests.rs:114`, changes the same process environment; OUT_DIR writers include `src/cache_key/tests.rs:5170`. The known test does not participate in that lock. Cwd changes also alter the root topology used at `src/compiler/cc.rs:5005` and 5077. That cwd participation is established by source inspection; an independent cwd-only failure was not forced.

The owner supplied one earlier full `just check` failure at line 295 and 3/3 isolated passes; those prior observations are not counted in this run ledger. The uninstrumented full suite reproduced a warm-key hash mismatch in R01 at 16 threads, load `{ 48.32 45.66 35.56 }`. A controlled SDKROOT removal between the baseline and first comparison failed in R05, and disabling normalization there failed in R07, both at one thread. No compiler, flag classifier, source file, or production key algorithm was changed. The baseline and comparison therefore genuinely used different ambient inputs. Relocating SDKROOT between two nonempty paths passed in R03, consistent with the SDK sentinel; the OUT_DIR-only probe passed in R06 and is not counted as proof of an OUT_DIR cause.

Reproduce on demand: `env KACHE_FLAKY_PROBE=SDKROOT ./scripts/with-test-resources.sh cargo test -p kache --bin kache terminal_formatting_shares_cc_keys_with_cold_and_warm_probes -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture` with phase-2 instrumentation and a nonempty initial SDKROOT; or substitute `KACHE_FLAKY_PROBE=NORMALIZE`. R04 and R13 were passing isolated controls. Natural and forced failure counts, with all later suite observations, are tabulated below.

The owner's historical pair of hashes cannot uniquely identify the writer or variable that changed; that run did not capture its key inputs. The proven explanation is that the test compares computations across mutable process state. SDKROOT removal and the normalization toggle are demonstrated sufficient causes, and a natural suite failure was reproduced. Attributing that particular historical event to one named sibling would require a trace of its inputs and writers.

Fix shape: hold the existing process-state lock for the entire comparison and establish explicit environment/cwd fixtures, or pass one environment/cwd snapshot through every computation. The assertion should vary diagnostic flags while keeping every other key input fixed.

Nonempty SDKROOT relocation was stable; isolated controls of the gated scheduler/wrapper/home tests passed. The rejected-meta wrapper test uses the same 200 ms sleep, but its final expected compile outcome also holds when the waiter starts late, so that sleep alone is not evidence it flakes. Download-waiter tests at `src/daemon/tests.rs:13708,13744,13861` combine notifications with map rechecks; no lost-wakeup failure was observed. The file-hash wall-clock observation test at `crates/kache-store/src/file_hash.rs:1137` brackets the observation with before/after samples rather than an elapsed speed requirement; it passed, though wall-clock adjustments were not induced. Phase tracing uses a thread-local recorder. Socket fixtures reviewed use unique temporary paths or ephemeral loopback ports, including `tests/fallback_recovery_test.rs:259` and `tests/s3_remote_test.rs:462`; no port collision, EMFILE, thread-exhaustion, or disk-exhaustion failure was observed. R01–R03 used `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/kache-flaky/sol/tmp`; R04–R18 used the worktree's `.flaky-tmp`; R19 onward use `/tmp/kache-flaky/sol/t`, whose resolved path is inside `/private/tmp/kache-flaky/sol/`. R18's 19 failures include `SUN_LEN` socket rejection and fixture paths accidentally inheriting the repository's workspace/toolchain roots; all disappeared in the serial run with the short outside-worktree alias. They are recorded as setup/path failures rather than timing/concurrency findings. No failure from those runs was silently converted into a timing finding.

R03/R04 were queued before earlier work finished; their isolated test processes overlapped briefly after build/package locks cleared. All subsequent test invocations were sequential. No process not started by this investigation was stopped or killed; R20 paused/resumed its own test process; R27 paused its own lsof child, which the existing timeout killed and reaped.

Seven tests have demonstrated dependencies on scheduling, the live process environment, or process-wide initialization. Two findings assert elapsed clock bounds, two use sleeps as synchronization, two depend on shared process state, and one assumes an optional external probe meets a deadline. The known cache-key failure is a shared-process-state race. The owner's clock hypothesis explains some findings, but does not explain all of them.

Investigation: detached `991c83694c056119d8eba8f9c1f376ac246efb52`, macOS arm64, one investigator, no subagents. No fixes, commits, pushes, PRs, issues, or mutation runs. Final `git diff --exit-code` and `git status --short` were clean. Temporary source instrumentation was restored; its complete diffs are included below. The report is saved at [report.md](/private/tmp/kache-flaky/sol/report.md); test logs and the run ledger are in the same directory. Test execution ran from 01:36:48 to 02:28:20 UTC on 2026-10-14, stopping at ten full-workspace commands.

All cargo invocations inherited `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/kache-flaky/sol/target`. The normal libtest default was 16 threads on this machine; explicit thread counts are recorded per run. The shell's soft nofile limit was 1,048,576, above the wrapper's 4,096 requirement. Load entries are the verbatim output of `sysctl -n vm.loadavg` immediately before each invocation, giving the 1-, 5-, and 15-minute averages; they are not measurements throughout the run.

For compact reproduction commands and the run table, `W` expands to `./scripts/with-test-resources.sh cargo test --workspace`, and `K` expands to `./scripts/with-test-resources.sh cargo test -p kache --bin kache`. Execute these from the worktree with the target directory exported. Commands requiring instrumentation use the corresponding patch below.

**1. Proven: `compiler::cc::tests::terminal_formatting_shares_cc_keys_with_cold_and_warm_probes`, [src/compiler/cc/tests.rs:250](/Users/viktor/Developer/github/kache-investigations/flaky-sol/src/compiler/cc/tests.rs:250). Class: shared process state, environment and current directory. Severity: high.**

The test computes the baseline at line 285 and compares cold and warm keys at lines 295 and 299 without taking the process-state lock. Every key reads ambient state again: `src/compiler/cc.rs:4389` builds its prefix-map identity from cwd, `KACHE_CC_PATH_NORMALIZE`, `KACHE_BASE_DIR`, `SDKROOT`, and `OUT_DIR`; line 4432 recomputes maps. A nonempty SDK contributes `/kache/sdkroot` at line 4628. Key generation hashes the distinct prefix-map sentinels at line 6933 and mapped source paths at line 7108. Changing normalization changes both of those inputs. The fake compiler at `tests/fixtures/mock_cc_diagnostics.sh:3` returns constant version/preprocessor output and echoes the already filtered probe arguments; it contains no clock-dependent output.

Sibling writers are concrete: `src/compiler/cc/tests.rs:6985` sets SDKROOT and line 6990 removes it; the environment/normalization test at line 7962 changes cwd, OUT_DIR, SDKROOT, and the normalization switch at lines 7983, 7996, and 8009. The shared lock at `src/test_support.rs:83` coordinates participating tests only. `set_env_for_test`, `src/config/tests.rs:114`, changes the same process environment; OUT_DIR writers include `src/cache_key/tests.rs:5170`. The known test does not participate in that lock. Cwd changes also alter the root topology used at `src/compiler/cc.rs:5005` and 5077. That cwd participation is established by source inspection; an independent cwd-only failure was not forced.

The owner supplied one earlier full `just check` failure at line 295 and 3/3 isolated passes; those prior observations are not counted in this run ledger. The uninstrumented full suite reproduced a warm-key hash mismatch in R01 at 16 threads, load `{ 48.32 45.66 35.56 }`. A controlled SDKROOT removal between the baseline and first comparison failed in R05, and disabling normalization there failed in R07, both at one thread. No fake-compiler script, flag classifier, C fixture content, or production key algorithm was changed. The baseline and comparison therefore genuinely used different ambient inputs. Relocating SDKROOT between two nonempty paths passed in R03, consistent with the SDK sentinel; the OUT_DIR-only probe passed in R06 and is not counted as proof of an OUT_DIR cause.

Reproduce on demand: `env KACHE_FLAKY_PROBE=SDKROOT ./scripts/with-test-resources.sh cargo test -p kache --bin kache terminal_formatting_shares_cc_keys_with_cold_and_warm_probes -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture` with phase-2 instrumentation and a nonempty initial SDKROOT; or substitute `KACHE_FLAKY_PROBE=NORMALIZE`. R04 and R13 were passing isolated controls. Natural and forced failure counts, with all later suite observations, are tabulated below.

The owner's historical pair of hashes cannot uniquely identify the writer or variable that changed; that run did not capture its key inputs. The proven explanation is that the test compares computations across mutable process state. SDKROOT removal and the normalization toggle are demonstrated sufficient causes, and a natural suite failure was reproduced. Attributing that particular historical event to one named sibling would require a trace of its inputs and writers.

Fix shape: hold the existing process-state lock for the entire comparison and establish explicit environment/cwd fixtures, or pass one environment/cwd snapshot through every computation. The assertion should vary diagnostic flags while keeping every other key input fixed.

**2. Proven: `scheduler::tests::permit_pool_blocks_until_a_slot_is_free`, [src/scheduler.rs:2335](/Users/viktor/Developer/github/kache-investigations/flaky-sol/src/scheduler.rs:2335). Class: scheduling-dependent clock assertion. Severity: medium.**

The child writes `lock-ready` and sleeps for 300 ms before exiting, `src/scheduler.rs:2651`. The parent observes readiness, then starts its measurement at line 2341. It asserts at least 50 ms elapsed at line 2349 and at least 50 ms added to the global wait counter at line 2353. Readiness establishes that the child held the permit when it wrote the file; it does not establish that the child still holds it when the parent is scheduled to acquire.

R08 forced the parent to resume after the child exited by waiting for that same child after readiness and before the original measurement. The permit was successfully acquired, but the original lower-bound assertion failed. This inserts no work into the measured operation and changes no scheduler behavior. It is the legal schedule where the parent loses its CPU slice long enough for the 300 ms holder to finish. Reproduce: `env KACHE_FLAKY_SCHEDULER=permit ./scripts/with-test-resources.sh cargo test -p kache --bin kache permit_pool_blocks_until_a_slot_is_free -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture`. One forced failure in one invocation; R14 was a passing serial control within the scheduler suite. Load in the forced run: `{ 43.84 66.49 50.05 }`.

Fix shape: keep the child permit held until an explicit release handshake, establish a failed/nonblocking acquisition while it is held, then release it and assert acquisition succeeds. Verify wait attribution with an isolated counter or a deterministic clock rather than the remaining duration of the child's sleep.

The test spawns a waiter at line 2311, sleeps 200 ms at line 2315, and releases the child through `go` at line 2316. The fixture writes the artifact and drops its lock at lines 2568–2569. The test requires `BeginMiss::Recheck` at line 2317, assuming the waiter has already tried the held lock. `Scheduler::join_flight`, `src/scheduler.rs:413`, legitimately returns ownership immediately if its first acquisition finds the lock free; only a failed initial acquisition followed by a release produces `FlightJoin::Waited` and the recheck path.

That is **not** counted as proof: the original default current-thread Tokio runtime has no yield between spawning the signal task and starting the timer. R20 preserves that original scheduling structure and proves the upper-bound problem by pausing the process externally.

Fix shape: establish a pending warming future, signal completion, and assert it resolves successfully. Exercise timeout behavior with virtual Tokio time or explicit clock input. The mechanism does not require a real-machine one-second speed assertion.

Class: external-tool deadline and a strict assertion on a best-effort probe. Severity: high; macOS only.**

The test proves its sandboxed listener accepts a TCP connection using a 30-second readiness budget at lines 276–284. It then requires the fallback to be bypassed, and `fixture.calls()` to be exactly `"direct\n"`, at line 320. The optional production preflight has an independent, much narrower budget: `src/fallback/macos.rs:38` starts `/usr/sbin/lsof`; line 57 starts a 200 ms deadline; lines 59–67 kill/reap an unfinished lsof and return `None`. `src/fallback/sandbox.rs:32` propagates that missing PID as an unknown policy. `src/fallback.rs:35` then takes its documented recovery path: try the fallback and, if it fails, compile directly. The test's listener-readiness condition does not ensure lsof completes within 200 ms.

R21 naturally failed the original call-sequence assertion in a 16-thread full run, load `{ 79.93 70.06 57.80 }`. R19 at one thread and R22 at 32 threads passed this target, so failure is not a monotonic function of thread count. R27 stopped only the lsof child that kache had just spawned, leaving the test's ready listener and all policy/timeout logic intact. The log records a successful SIGSTOP, expiry of the 200 ms deadline, and the same original assertion failure: `"fallback\ndirect\n"` instead of `"direct\n"`. item.text:
Seven tests have demonstrated dependencies on scheduling, the live process environment, or process-wide initialization. Two findings assert elapsed clock bounds, two use sleeps as synchronization, two depend on shared process state, and one assumes an optional external probe meets a deadline. The known cache-key failure is a shared-process-state race. The owner's clock hypothesis explains some findings, but does not explain all of them.

Investigation: detached `991c83694c056119d8eba8f9c1f376ac246efb52`, macOS arm64, one investigator, no subagents. No fixes, commits, pushes, PRs, issues, or mutation runs. Final `git diff --exit-code` and `git status --short` were clean. Temporary source instrumentation was restored; its complete diffs are included below. The report is saved at [report.md](/private/tmp/kache-flaky/sol/report.md); test logs and the run ledger are in the same directory. Test execution ran from 01:36:48 to 02:28:20 UTC on 2026-10-14, stopping at ten full-workspace commands.

All cargo invocations inherited `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/kache-flaky/sol/target`. The normal libtest default was 16 threads on this machine; explicit thread counts are recorded per run. The shell's soft nofile limit was 1,048,576, above the wrapper's 4,096 requirement. Load entries are the verbatim output of `sysctl -n vm.loadavg` immediately before each invocation, giving the 1-, 5-, and 15-minute averages; they are not measurements throughout the run.

For compact reproduction commands and the run table, `W` expands to `./scripts/with-test-resources.sh cargo test --workspace`, and `K` expands to `./scripts/with-test-resources.sh cargo test -p kache --bin kache`. Execute these from the worktree with the target directory exported. Commands requiring instrumentation use the corresponding patch below.

**1. Proven: `compiler::cc::tests::terminal_formatting_shares_cc_keys_with_cold_and_warm_probes`, [src/compiler/cc/tests.rs:250](/Users/viktor/Developer/github/kache-investigations/flaky-sol/src/compiler/cc/tests.rs:250). Class: shared process state, environment and current directory. Severity: high.**

The test computes the baseline at line 285 and compares cold and warm keys at lines 295 and 299 without taking the process-state lock. Every key reads ambient state again: `src/compiler/cc.rs:4389` builds its prefix-map identity from cwd, `KACHE_CC_PATH_NORMALIZE`, `KACHE_BASE_DIR`, `SDKROOT`, and `OUT_DIR`; line 4432 recomputes maps. A nonempty SDK contributes `/kache/sdkroot` at line 4628. Key generation hashes the distinct prefix-map sentinels at line 6933 and mapped source paths at line 7108. Changing normalization changes both of those inputs. The fake compiler at `tests/fixtures/mock_cc_diagnostics.sh:3` returns constant version/preprocessor output and echoes the already filtered probe arguments; it contains no clock-dependent output.

Sibling writers are concrete: `src/compiler/cc/tests.rs:6985` sets SDKROOT and line 6990 removes it; the environment/normalization test at line 7962 changes cwd, OUT_DIR, SDKROOT, and the normalization switch at lines 7983, 7996, and 8009. The shared lock at `src/test_support.rs:83` coordinates participating tests only. `set_env_for_test`, `src/config/tests.rs:114`, changes the same process environment; OUT_DIR writers include `src/cache_key/tests.rs:5170`. The known test does not participate in that lock. Cwd changes also alter the root topology used at `src/compiler/cc.rs:5005` and 5077. That cwd participation is established by source inspection; an independent cwd-only failure was not forced.

The owner supplied one earlier full `just check` failure at line 295 and 3/3 isolated passes; those prior observations are not counted in this run ledger. The uninstrumented full suite reproduced a warm-key hash mismatch in R01 at 16 threads, load `{ 48.32 45.66 35.56 }`. A controlled SDKROOT removal between the baseline and first comparison failed in R05, and disabling normalization there failed in R07, both at one thread. No fake-compiler script, flag classifier, C fixture content, or production key algorithm was changed. The baseline and comparison therefore genuinely used different ambient inputs. Relocating SDKROOT between two nonempty paths passed in R03, consistent with the SDK sentinel; the OUT_DIR-only probe passed in R06 and is not counted as proof of an OUT_DIR cause.

Reproduce on demand: `env KACHE_FLAKY_PROBE=SDKROOT ./scripts/with-test-resources.sh cargo test -p kache --bin kache terminal_formatting_shares_cc_keys_with_cold_and_warm_probes -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture` with phase-2 instrumentation and a nonempty initial SDKROOT; or substitute `KACHE_FLAKY_PROBE=NORMALIZE`. R04 and R13 were passing isolated controls. Natural and forced failure counts, with all later suite observations, are tabulated below.

The owner's historical pair of hashes cannot uniquely identify the writer or variable that changed; that run did not capture its key inputs. The proven explanation is that the test compares computations across mutable process state. SDKROOT removal and the normalization toggle are demonstrated sufficient causes, and a natural suite failure was reproduced. Attributing that particular historical event to one named sibling would require a trace of its inputs and writers.

Fix shape: hold the existing process-state lock for the entire comparison and establish explicit environment/cwd fixtures, or pass one environment/cwd snapshot through every computation. The assertion should vary diagnostic flags while keeping every other key input fixed.

**2. Proven: `scheduler::tests::permit_pool_blocks_until_a_slot_is_free`, [src/scheduler.rs:2335](/Users/viktor/Developer/github/kache-investigations/flaky-sol/src/scheduler.rs:2335). Class: scheduling-dependent clock assertion. Severity: medium.**

The child writes `lock-ready` and sleeps for 300 ms before exiting, `src/scheduler.rs:2651`. The parent observes readiness, then starts its measurement at line 2341. It asserts at least 50 ms elapsed at line 2349 and at least 50 ms added to the global wait counter at line 2353. Readiness establishes that the child held the permit when it wrote the file; it does not establish that the child still holds it when the parent is scheduled to acquire.

R08 forced the parent to resume after the child exited by waiting for that same child after readiness and before the original measurement. The permit was successfully acquired, but the original lower-bound assertion failed. This inserts no work into the measured operation and changes no scheduler behavior. It is the legal schedule where the parent loses its CPU slice long enough for the 300 ms holder to finish. Reproduce: `env KACHE_FLAKY_SCHEDULER=permit ./scripts/with-test-resources.sh cargo test -p kache --bin kache permit_pool_blocks_until_a_slot_is_free -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture`. One forced failure in one invocation; R14 was a passing serial control within the scheduler suite. Load in the forced run: `{ 43.84 66.49 50.05 }`.

Fix shape: keep the child permit held until an explicit release handshake, establish a failed/nonblocking acquisition while it is held, then release it and assert acquisition succeeds. Verify wait attribution with an isolated counter or a deterministic clock rather than the remaining duration of the child's sleep.

```text
thread 'scheduler::tests::permit_pool_blocks_until_a_slot_is_free' (147862733) panicked at src/scheduler.rs:2359:9:
parent must have waited for the child-held slot
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
```

**3. Proven: `scheduler::tests::waiter_rechecks_after_owner_completes`, [src/scheduler.rs:2300](/Users/viktor/Developer/github/kache-investigations/flaky-sol/src/scheduler.rs:2300). Class: nondeterministic thread scheduling and sleep used as synchronization. Severity: medium.**

The test spawns a waiter at line 2311, sleeps 200 ms at line 2315, and releases the child through `go` at line 2316. The fixture writes the artifact and drops its lock at lines 2568–2569. The test requires `BeginMiss::Recheck` at line 2317, assuming the waiter has already tried the held lock. `Scheduler::join_flight`, `src/scheduler.rs:413`, legitimately returns ownership immediately if its first acquisition finds the lock free; only a failed initial acquisition followed by a release produces `FlightJoin::Waited` and the recheck path.

R09 gated the waiter before its original `begin_miss`, released and joined the existing child, and only then let the waiter execute. The original assertion failed with `Compile`, while the owner's artifact had already been written. The 200 ms sleep supplies no happens-before relationship with the waiter's first lock attempt. Reproduce: `env KACHE_FLAKY_SCHEDULER=flight ./scripts/with-test-resources.sh cargo test -p kache --bin kache waiter_rechecks_after_owner_completes -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture`. One forced failure in one invocation; R14 passed without the gate. Forced-run load: `{ 43.84 66.49 50.05 }`.

Fix shape: acknowledge the waiter's failed acquisition before allowing the owner to publish/release, then assert the subsequent recheck and artifact visibility. An explicit handshake must replace the assumption that a spawned thread ran within 200 ms.

second process must wait for the in-flight owner
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
```

**4. Proven: `wrapper::tests::admit_scheduler_miss_recheck_returns_accepted_meta`, [src/wrapper/tests.rs:10603](/Users/viktor/Developer/github/kache-investigations/flaky-sol/src/wrapper/tests.rs:10603). Class: nondeterministic thread scheduling and sleep used as synchronization. Severity: medium.**

This has the same schedule dependency at a distinct wrapper boundary. It spawns its waiter at line 10614, sleeps 200 ms at line 10627, releases the fixture at line 10628, then requires an empty guard and a cache hit at lines 10630–10635. The child drops its scheduler guard at line 10694. `admit_scheduler_miss`, `src/wrapper.rs:1123`, consults the cached metadata only on `BeginMiss::Recheck` at line 1145; an immediately acquired flight returns `(guard, None)` at line 1150.

R12 held the waiter before the original wrapper call, released and joined the existing owner, then admitted the waiter. It returned the compile guard, failing the original assertion. Reproduce: `env KACHE_FLAKY_WRAPPER=1 ./scripts/with-test-resources.sh cargo test -p kache --bin kache admit_scheduler_miss_recheck_returns_accepted_meta -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture`. One forced failure in one invocation; R17 passed without the gate. Forced-run load: `{ 43.84 66.49 50.05 }`.

Fix shape: prove the waiter encountered the held flight before permitting release. Then assert the accepted metadata and released guard at the wrapper boundary, using the owner/waiter handshake rather than elapsed sleep.

thread 'wrapper::tests::admit_scheduler_miss_recheck_returns_accepted_meta' (147863750) panicked at src/wrapper/tests.rs:10637:5:
a Recheck hit must not keep the flight or permit
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
```

**5. Proven: `cli::tests::test_is_macos_protected`, [src/cli/tests.rs:2823](/Users/viktor/Developer/github/kache-investigations/flaky-sol/src/cli/tests.rs:2823). Class: shared process state and order-dependent global initialization. Severity: medium; macOS only.**

`is_macos_protected`, `src/cli.rs:6209`, caches its prefix list in a process-wide `OnceLock` at line 6212. Its first call uses `dirs::home_dir()` at line 6223. The test later obtains the current home at `src/cli/tests.rs:2847` and expects that home's Desktop to be protected at line 2848. Those home values need not agree. Existing sibling code temporarily replaces HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME in `KunobiConfigGuard::new`, `src/test_support.rs:109`, and restores them on drop at line 132. A lock cannot retroactively repair a OnceLock initialized under a temporary home by an uncoordinated reader.

R11 initialized the existing prefix cache with a temporary HOME, restored HOME through the existing guard, and ran the original assertions. The Desktop assertion failed. No cache implementation was modified. Reproduce in a fresh process: `env KACHE_FLAKY_HOME=1 ./scripts/with-test-resources.sh cargo test -p kache --bin kache test_is_macos_protected -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture`. One forced failure in one invocation; R16 passed in a fresh process without that initialization. Forced-run load: `{ 43.84 66.49 50.05 }`.

Fix shape: test the classification core with explicit home/prefix inputs; test process-wide initialization in isolated subprocesses with a deliberately fixed HOME. Comparing a cache initialized by an earlier caller against the current ambient HOME leaves run order in the oracle.

thread 'cli::tests::test_is_macos_protected' (147863622) panicked at src/cli/tests.rs:2853:9:
assertion failed: is_macos_protected(&home.join("Desktop"))
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
```

**6. Proven: `daemon::tests::test_wait_for_warming_blocks_then_signals`, [src/daemon/tests.rs:10544](/Users/viktor/Developer/github/kache-investigations/flaky-sol/src/daemon/tests.rs:10544). Class: wall-clock upper-bound assertion under descheduling. Severity: medium.**

The signal task sleeps 50 ms at line 10551. The waiter has a five-second grace at line 10556, but the test also requires elapsed time below one second at line 10560. `wait_for_warming`, `src/daemon.rs:3268`, returns the watch-channel completion state, or observes a change under the requested timeout. A CPU scheduling pause can consume the test's one-second allowance without breaking that mechanism or exhausting the five-second grace.

R20 emitted a PID marker immediately after the original timer started, then the external controller sent SIGSTOP only to that test process, waited 1.2 seconds, and sent SIGCONT. The existing warming-result assertion passed, and the existing `elapsed < 1s` assertion failed. Reproduce by applying phase-3 instrumentation and running `python3 /private/tmp/kache-flaky/sol/run.py R20-repro python3 /private/tmp/kache-flaky/sol/suspend.py`. The controller invokes `env KACHE_FLAKY_SUSPEND=1 ./scripts/with-test-resources.sh cargo test -p kache --bin kache test_wait_for_warming_blocks_then_signals -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture`.
